Thanks again for the catch-up yesterday. Attaching the latest Order Form draft we discussed (v3). Key commercial points we want to flag for transparency before your legal/proc team redlines:

- Minimum commit phasing: we propose a 3-tranche ramp (30/30/40) across Q4–Q1 to match your expected usage.

Please have Procurement and Legal send any specific redlines back to me — if you prefer, send a marked PDF or track changes doc. If withholding is a hard requirement we may need to split the invoice flows by legal entity (two invoices) or agree a gross-up clause.

3) Invoice recipient & entity: we need invoices issued to Horizon Health, Inc. (billing@horizonhealth.com) and will attach a PO.
4) Evidence: Legal requests confirmation of Redwood's tax residency, VAT registration (if applicable), and a contact in finance for statements.

I've attached our marked redline PDF (HH_OrderForm_v3_procurement_redlines.pdf). Please route to Finance and Legal so we can get this wrapped in the next 7–10 business days — our procurement window closes 09/17.

Team —

Thanks for flagging, Mateo. Quick internal position and recommended path to hit procurement window:

1) Net terms: accept net 45 contractually; offer a 1%/net 30 early-pay discount as a commercial sweetener. Rationale: net 60 materially increases DSO and is outside standard Enterprise policy unless elevated. If Finance will sign off we can present net45 + early-pay to Horizon.

2) Withholding/tax: propose two parallel options to present to Horizon — (A) Redwood provides a tax residency certificate and accepts the 2% withholding (we will net against gross and provide a residency letter), or (B) invoicing split: Redwood issues two invoices mapped to distinct Redwood legal entities (Service invoice to Redwood, Inc.; Maintenance to Redwood US Holdings) to reduce withholding exposure. Option B requires Procurement to accept two invoices and two remit-to addresses.

3) Billing entity & PO: require PO on file for minimum commit tranches. We can accept a single PO referencing the Order Form and indicate invoicing split in an appendix.

4) Suggested language: I've attached a short proposed clause for the order form (Proposed_Billing_Split.docx) and our internal tax matrix (Redwood_TaxMatrix.xlsx). Karthik — please advise whether the proposed clause needs any legal tightening (indemnity, gross-up triggers).

If Finance signs off on net45 + early-pay, I recommend we send Sophie a concise email with the two withholding options and a DocuSign link for the revised order form. Call to action: Sophie needs a proposal by 09/09 to stay within their window.

-Kim

Thanks for the redlines and fast turnaround. After internal review here's our compromise to keep you inside the procurement window:

- Net terms: Redwood can accept net 45 contractually. In exchange, we will provide a 1% discount if Horizon pays within 30 days. This is our operational ceiling without CFO approval.
- Withholding: we can accept the 2% statutory withholding if Horizon provides the standard withholding form. Alternatively, we can implement Option B (invoice split) if Procurement confirms both entities and remit-to addresses.
- Billing entity: we will issue invoices to Horizon Health, Inc. as requested. For the split-invoice approach, we'll include a separate remit-to appendix and require a PO that references which tranche(s) are being prepaid.
- Evidence: attached is a Redwood tax residency letter (summary) and the Tax Matrix for your counsel. For final execution we will provide the formal residency certificate prior to first invoice.

I've attached an updated Order Form (v3.1) with the net45/early-pay language and both withholding options shown as alternatives in an appendix. Please confirm which withholding path Horizon prefers and whether you'll issue the PO by 09/14 so we can schedule the first tranche invoice for 09/30.
